title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 430
paragraphs: These were the acts of madness done by Cambyses toward those of his own family, whether his madness was produced really on account of Apis or from some other cause, as many ills are wont to seize upon men; for it is said, moreover, that Cambyses had from birth a certain grievous malady — the one called by some the “sacred” disease. And it was certainly nothing strange that, when the body was suffering from a grievous malady, the mind should not be sound either.
